items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: Oliver Coleman, my very dear friend.

ctx.x: Yes, unfortunately, yes. But the man that - Hamilton, he was playing with Paul Whiteman's band, so they'd say, 'Hi-boy.' Before then it was down on the floor and Cuba Austin had this little thing where you used to slide your foot in. It had a little overlapping thing and then they made a little short one. I have one and then he'd go down and.... at the shop... But then they didn't have it up here. As recent as 1934 when I told you I stood down and saw you with Erskine Tate when I came from the World's Fair,…
There was another great drummer around Chicago that we thought a lot of. I just wanted to ask you, did you ever run into Oliver Coleman?

Please, you know that was O.C., that was my friend and I gave him a secret and fortunately for him - it's rather difficult for a person to instruct and teach music at the same time and to have pupils that can come out and be a credit to him. Because you know you can go to Harvard, Dartmouth, and Yale. You can go to Eton. I don't care where you go. You can go anywhere in the world,
